correctness.rationale: For each d, exchangeability under DOMAIN-POSITION permutations makes the image assignment a uniform rearrangement of a multiset with multiplicities d_i. For r distinct requested diagonal hits, the without-replacement probability is product d_i/(n)_r, and summing over r-tuples gives E[(F)_r|d]=r!e_r(d)/(n)_r. The elementary symmetric count e_r(d)<=C(n,r) yields each factorial moment <=1 and uniformly controls all positive exponential moments. For sorted normalized d_i/n=a_ni, a_ni<=1/i and sum_{i>K}a_ni²<=1/(K+1); thus H_n(z)=product_i(1+a_ni z) converges locally uniformly to exp(qz) product_j(1+p_j z) along coordinatewise convergent profiles. The exact falling-factorial normalization tends to 1 at fixed r, uniform factorial-moment domination permits passage to the entire probability-generating function, and discrete atom convergence plus Scheffe yields TOTAL VARIATION convergence. Variance [n²-sum d_i²]/[n(n-1)] plus uniform exponential integrability proves Poisson(1) implies max d_i/n->0; diffuse degrees prove the converse. Diagonal compactness and explicit floor-and-even-residual integer allocations realize every admissible p_j family. Independent exact enumeration of all 50,069 maps at n=1..6 across 637 degree profiles verifies every full finite conditional distribution, moments, mean and variance; four n=600 profile-moment checks corroborate the boundary limits. The n=1 case is deterministic F=1, and the variance formula is explicitly restricted to n>=2. Finite experiments are not used as the proof of infinite limits.

value.rationale: The complete labelled indegree sequence is a natural observable of finite functional digraphs, and the conditional number of loops is a canonical statistic. While the invariant conditional mean 1 is elementary, the result gives an exact full finite conditional law, a complete class of all possible TV subsequential limit distributions with macroscopic indegree hubs, a necessary AND sufficient sharp Poisson(1) criterion, and realizability of every admissible Poisson-plus-Bernoulli profile. This distinguishes diffuse-degree Poisson behavior from qualitatively non-Poisson concentrated-degree behavior and constitutes a motivated classification rather than a one-moment exercise or arbitrary numerical gain. The theorem is limited to exchangeable image-coordinate laws and does not claim rates or nonexchangeable extensions; no downstream paper-sized application is needed for its mathematical value.
